description: Seed of the fastener-library stream (DRAFT_tolerance_stack_mvp groundwork item 1), now also holding vendor bearings under Joby source-control drawings. Every entry carries INLINE values and a `values_source` saying where those numbers came from -- a source_ref-shaped dict, mandatory whenever `values_status == "inline"` and explicitly null when it is `not_transcribed`. READ IT BEFORE REUSING A BAND: eight of the fifteen entries transcribe the 260729 workbook (with parts-list nomenclature corroborating some nominals), which makes those numbers UNUSABLE as a source in a from-scratch stack -- citing the entry instead of the xlsx launders the same untraced value (SOP Step 5b, trap 17). THREE entries are traced and safe to reuse: NAS6403U11D, traced to the NAS6403 standard in the spec pile; and 214589-002 / 214588-002, traced to their own source-control drawings, where the drawing IS the controlling document for the vendor part and prints its limits directly. Four entries are `not_transcribed` with `values_source: null`. Counts in this paragraph are asserted by tests/test_tolerance_stack.py::test_hardware_entry_values_source_counts_match_the_description, because a count written in prose goes stale silently. `library_ref` is the slot a real library entry drops into; when it is filled, `values_status` moves from `inline` to `library` and the inline numbers become a cross-check rather than the source.

values_source.note: The ONLY entry in this file whose inline numbers come from the actual standard rather than from the 260729 workbook or a parts list. `hardware_entry/v0` had no field for citing where inline values came from, so `values_source` was added as an additive extension by handoff pitch_link_stack -- see LESSONS_20260804_pitch_link_stack.md -- and made mandatory-for-inline by handoff sop_edits_apply, which also renamed this dict's `sheets` key to `sheet` so it matches SourceRef. gaps: The THREAD RUN-OUT / incomplete-thread length is still not sourced. NAS6403 dimensions grip (to the end of the full cylindrical shank) and length (to the point) and gives T = .323 in as a reference between them, but never dimensions the transition itself. So slice 1's 1/16 in 'thread transition allowance' remains an uncited rule of thumb; the document that would close it is MIL-S-8879 (the thread spec sheet 1 invokes for UNJF-3A), which is not in data/inbox/specs/.

Sheet 5 of 5 is MISSING from the PDF. Sheet 1's LIST OF CURRENT SHEETS names five sheets (1 rev 4, 2 rev 2, 3 NEW, 4 rev 2, 5 rev 3); the file holds four. Nothing this stack uses lives on sheet 5, but a library ingest must not assume the file is complete.
The MEANING of dimension M (.174/.154) is read off the sheet-1 figure's extension lines, not from any text -- the standard never defines M in words. Highest-value item for a second reader to confirm.

Grip tolerance and length tolerance are folded here as independent variates. They are not: T = length - grip is a reference dimension, so the worst-case spread on `thread_region_T` (7.5692 .. 8.8392) is wider than the real part can be. Whether the standard controls length, grip, or both as the independent feature is not stated.

The BAND is the workbook's row 67, `under head chamfer washer`: G67 `=(0.057)*25.4`, H67 `=(0.069)*25.4`, E67 `=(G67+H67)/2` -- i.e. .063 +/-.006, stated as limits and never as a tolerance. Note the workbook never labels row 67 as this part: its comment column names MS21299C4K at I64, the SPHERICAL BEARING row, and that column is a loose hardware list rather than a row-aligned one (slice-1 F5), so even the attribution of the band to this washer is a reading. MS21299 is not in the spec pile. Not usable as a source in a from-scratch stack (SOP Step 5b).

assembly_status.note: NOT CHECKED against 217755. This stack was built from the part drawings and the workbook; the assembly export was not opened, so present/find_no/qty are null rather than guessed. Listed as a gap.

gaps: The bore (160.000 0/-0.018) is traced and DELIBERATELY UNUSED: the bearing-bore-to-spindle fit is outside this stack's scope (Jeff, 2026-08-05 -- a separate team owns that joint). Recorded so a later stack that does sweep it in does not have to re-read the drawing.

MATERIAL NOT STATED. The drawing is a source control drawing and names no material; the workbook's '52100' is the only source for it, and it is untraced. Needs the NSK material certificate (which drawing note 6 requires per lot/serial) or JED01848 (Propulsion Bearing Engineering Specification), which the drawing cites and which is not in data/inbox/specs/. This is what blocks the bearing CTE -- see materials.json.

JED01848 is not in the spec pile. It determines load capacity AND operating temperature per drawing note 3, so it is also the document most likely to state the qualified hot-case temperature that the workbook's 72 C stands in for.
Presence, find number, quantity and balloons on 217755 not checked -- the assembly export was not opened by this handoff.

Outer-ring radial thickness and stiffness are not on the drawing, so whether the ring itself deflects under the fit interference cannot be assessed. A bearing supplier question, not a tolerance one, but it bounds how literally the stage-2 numbers can be read.

This bearing is GREASE PACKED -- 'EA6 GREASE. GREASE AMOUNT: (35% FILL), 7.7g +/-1g' (note 3), which the lower bearing's drawing does not say. JPS00078 caps shrink-fit heating at 80 C for bearings with shields or seals against 120 C without, so whether this one has seals changes the assembly process window. Not a tolerance question; recorded because it is the kind of thing that decides HOW the interference gets achieved.
